{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Turkey|Cuisine of Turkey]]

'''Börek''' is a general term in Turkish cuisine that applies to a family of [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastries]] with about fifty different members.  They have in common the fact that they are all pastry layers of some type enclosing a filling. There are two basic methods; one consists of rolling out very thin sheets of dough, called [[w:en:yufka|yufka]] in Turkish and [[w:en:phyllo|phyllo]] in Greek. The other main type of börek, called ''[[w:en:nemse börek|nemse börek]]'' in Turkish, uses a dough very similar to ''[[Cookbook:Puff pastry|pâte feuilletée]]'', in which the dough is layered with butter, folded, and rolled out several times.<ref>Algar, Ayla Esen (1985) ''The Complete Book of Turkish Cooking'' {{#isbn:0-710-30334-3}}</ref>

The following recipe describes the procedure required to prepare triangle-shaped börek from commercially produced phyllo. Links to recipes for fillings are listed at the end of the recipe.

==Ingredients==

=== Fillings ===
*[[Cookbook:Cheese Filling for Peynirli Börek|Peynirli börek]] (white cheese filling)
*Kıymalı börek (minced meat filling)
*Tavuklu börek (chicken filling)
*Ispanaklı börek (spinach filling)

=== Assembly ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] prepared filling (see above)
* 1 box yufka/[[Cookbook:Phyllo Dough|phyllo]] pastry sheets<ref>Available from Turkish, Greek, Armenian and Middle-Eastern grocers, among others, as well as some supermarkets.</ref>
* Melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or high-quality [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]<ref>e.g. peanut, hazelnut, walnut, almond, grapeseed. Avoid anything with a greasy taste such as corn oil.</ref>
[[Image:Wrapping börek.jpg|thumbnail|right|250px|Assembling börek triangles]]
==Procedure==
#Remove the phyllo sheets from the container. Unfold carefully so as not to break them. Lay them flat and cover with a clean, damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out—this is important.
# Working quickly, cut the phyllo into lengthwise thirds (step 1 in the diagram). Lay one of these out and cover the other two with the damp tea towel.
# Brush the strip of phyllo with the melted butter. Place a heaped [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoonful]] of filling on one end of the strip (step 2 in the diagram).
#Fold the right lower corner upward over the filling to form a triangle (step 3 in the diagram).
#Now fold the right upper corner over to the left (step 4 in the diagram).
#Continue folding in this manner until you reach the end of the strip.
#Trim of any excess dough and seal the edges by rubbing a damp finger over the dough and pressing the edge of the triangle where the strip ends.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] in oil at 340°F until golden brown or [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 350°F for 15 minutes.<ref>Prewrapped, uncooked börek freezes well. To cook, bake at 325ºF for 30 minutes.  Do not deep-fry frozen foods.  Splattering oil can cause burns and fires.  You may sautée them in a covered pan 2 or 3 at a time.  Hold the cover in front of your face as you place each börek in the pan.</ref>

==Notes==
